clue.text: Glass apt to shatter in extremis

indicators.note: glass that shatters breaks into pieces, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A pane of glass liable to break at the slightest extra strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shatter' rearranges GLASS and APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A final effort made at the point of death or collapse is one made in extremis, Latin for 'in the utmost straits'.

clue.text: Celebrate, seeing double when getting up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

explanation.surface: Someone celebrating so hard they see double when they stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when getting up' reverses DUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly, honouring or celebrating someone.

clue.text: Such pomposity is by no means a front

definitions.meaning: ... is dated British slang for airs and graces, as in 'putting on ...'
a flank is distinct from the front

explanation.surface: Pretentious airs are hardly a convincing facade.
explanation.walkthrough: Front looks like a pretence, but here it is the face of something opposed to its flank.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: dated slang for haughty airs, and the flank of something as opposed to its front.

clue.text: Such tactics used to combat brute's speech?

indicators.note: speech means the sound of a word when spoken

parts.note: a gorilla is a large and powerful ape, a brute

explanation.surface: Fighting tactics to counter an animal's language.
explanation.walkthrough: GORILLA spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit-and-run tactics by irregular fighters are the guerrilla kind, used in combat.

clue.text: One who is out and about

definitions.text: One who is out and about

parts.words: One who is out and about
parts.note: out means asleep here, so someone wandering around while unconscious

explanation.surface: A busy person always active and around town.
explanation.walkthrough: Out and about suggests sociable, but 'out' means asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepwalker moves around while still asleep, fully out yet walking about.

clue.text: Believe only one side of the account

definitions.meaning: to give credence to, trust as true

definitions.text: only one side of the account
definitions.meaning: in bookkeeping the right-hand column of a ledger, opposite the debit side

explanation.surface: Someone trusts just half of a story they have been told.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a verb meaning trust, and the accounting column for sums received.

clue.text: Concerning the first woman magistrate of long ago

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: About the first female judge of past times.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or magistrate in Anglo-Saxon and medieval England.

clue.text: Be unlucky in raffle, but lucky in Russian roulette

definitions.meaning: to pull out a ticket that wins nothing
a chamber with no bullet when the trigger is pulled

explanation.surface: A loss in a prize draw is a win in a deadly game.
explanation.walkthrough: In a raffle you pick a losing ticket; in Russian roulette the gun fires no bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fail or come away empty-handed; literally, firing an empty cartridge.

clue.text: Watch, perhaps, how punctual one is?

definitions.meaning: a wristwatch is one device that keeps track of the hour
a reliable person keeps to time

explanation.surface: Asking how reliable someone's watch is.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or watch records the hours; a referee or punctual person also keeps the hours.

clue.text: Unforeseen turn made badly

indicators.note: something made badly is put together wrongly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A surprise twist in events that was badly carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TURN and MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never imagined, not even dreamt of, was not foreseen: a near synonym.

clue.text: Still good advice to the overexcited

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to quieten or make motionless
the phrase read as two words, an instruction to settle down

explanation.surface: Calm down: sound counsel for anyone getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE CALM, it is what you would tell someone too excited.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm is to make still, as wind dropping leaves a sailing ship motionless.

clue.text: House address that's particularly exclusive

parts.note: a house is a theatre audience, and an address is a speech to it supposedly private but heard by all

explanation.surface: A posh residential address.
explanation.walkthrough: House and address suggest property; a theatre's house hears an aside meant to seem secret. 'Exclusive' is ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's loud aside, meant for the audience yet supposedly unheard by others on stage.

clue.text: Ruin the riverside, as punters may do

definitions.meaning: read literally, to breach the bank of a river
punters here are gamblers, who may win all the money a casino holds

explanation.surface: Boaters on the river damage its bank with their poles.
explanation.walkthrough: Punters look like people in punts on a river, but they are gamblers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler who wins more than the casino can pay is said to break the bank; the other sense is a literal breach of a riverbank.

clue.text: Exciting habit

definitions.meaning: the nervous practice of chewing fingertips

explanation.surface: A thrilling custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a nervous habit of chewing one's fingertips and a cliffhanger tense enough to cause it.

clue.text: Deal with spin to make a powerful stroke to off

parts.note: to cover a topic is to deal with it
a spin in a car is a drive

explanation.surface: Coping with a spinning ball to play a strong shot on the off side, in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Spin looks like cricket spin bowling, but it is an outing in a car. In cricket the off side is the batsman's facing side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a cover drive is a forceful shot hit through the covers on the off side.

clue.text: A charge to go across an island?

parts.note: a toll is a fee charged for passage, as on a bridge or road

explanation.surface: A fee payable to cross over to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island; the question mark admits the definition is broad.

clue.text: Pretty girl clinging on to an arm in game at the tables?

indicators.note: the girl holds on round the arm, so her letters wrap the other piece

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
an gives the letter A
gat is slang for a gun, a firearm

explanation.surface: An attractive woman holds a man's arm while playing at a gaming table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clinging on to' signals the container. Arm looks like a limb but is American slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a game played on a table, rolling balls into holes, a cousin of billiards.

clue.text: With everything to throw around there's nothing left

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around has the throw placed on either side of everything

parts.note: to toss is to throw
all means everything

explanation.surface: Throwing everything away leaves you with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; the throw wraps everything, and the plain 'to' leads.
explanation.definitionFit: When a write-off leaves nothing salvageable, as in insurance, it is complete destruction.

clue.text: Willingly permit to remain inactive

parts.note: lief is an old word meaning gladly or willingly
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: Gladly letting something stay idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Land left unplanted for a season rests; the idiom extends to anything left resting.

clue.text: Drawn so as to be perfect?

definitions.meaning: in grammar the perfect is a form of the verb denoting completed action

explanation.surface: Someone is strained by their effort to be flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: Perfect seems to mean flawless, but it is a grammatical category.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight and anxious is one sense; a verb form expressing time, like the perfect, is the other.

clue.text: It's being idle that can be hard to stomach

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Laziness is a habit others find difficult to tolerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges IT'S BEING IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that cannot be digested is hard on the stomach; it also means unacceptable figuratively.

clue.text: Pull up, to go over church in the valley

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lug is to pull or haul

explanation.surface: Stop and climb up to see the church in the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LUG to give GUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulch is a narrow, steep-sided ravine or valley, chiefly American.

clue.text: Senile and repetitive state

indicators.note: repetitive means the piece is given twice

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone senile repeating themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repetitive' doubles GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for being in one's dotage, mentally confused through old age.

clue.text: Satisfied with a quarter meaproperty sure

annotationWithheld.clue: Satisfied with a quarter meaproperty sure

clue.text: It may be suspended following freezing conditions

definitions.text: It may be suspended following freezing conditions

parts.words: It may be suspended following freezing conditions
parts.note: something hangs down after a hard frost, as from gutters, rather than a postponed event

explanation.surface: An event called off after an icy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspended suggests postponed, as a match after frost, but it means hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapering spike of frozen dripping water hangs from eaves after a frost.

clue.text: Pat, due to makeover, is now in fashion

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: After a makeover, Pat is finally stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makeover' rearranges PAT and DUE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Current and modern; something fashionable is right up to the present day.

clue.text: German writer apparently massaging the ego

indicators.note: massage works and kneads things, so these letters are kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: A German author seemingly flattering his own vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'massaging' rearranges THE EGO; massaging the ego looks like flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, author of Faust, is Germany's most famous writer.

clue.text: A proliferation of inernational gun-runners?

parts.note: imagines nations as competitors in a race to pile up weapons

explanation.surface: Illegal arms dealing spreading across the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'inernational' for international. Gun-runners suggests smugglers, but here it is countries racing to build weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition between states to build ever larger stocks of weapons, as in the Cold War.
